prompt: After a network change, same-node Service traffic works, cross-node traffic times out, and external Gateway requests intermittently return 503. Lead the incident.
directAnswer: Declare impact, freeze network/route changes, bind cluster/CNI/dataplane/Gateway versions and exact source/backend UIDs/nodes/five-tuples. Prove DNS and route attachment separately. Compare direct Pod and ClusterIP paths from same/cross nodes, EndpointSlice locality, policy directions, node routes, encapsulation, MTU, firewall, conntrack and return path. Correlate Gateway 503 backend/revision evidence with endpoint locality. Roll back the owning network change when risk warrants, never hand-edit node rules without ownership. Verify cross-node internal and normal external TLS/Host/path requests across endpoints, plus denied policy controls.
foundation: Path asymmetry localizes node/underlay/dataplane boundaries while 503 is a later gateway symptom.
reasoningSteps: Inspect routes MTU firewall conntrack return.
Add cross-node synthetic and change guard.
seniorAnswer: I use the working same-node path as a control and avoid indiscriminate restarts. The cross-node delta focuses overlay/underlay, MTU, node rules, CNI health and return routing; Gateway 503 is correlated to which backends/nodes were selected. Recovery is owner-level rollback and multi-path user verification.
weakAnswer: Increase Gateway timeouts and restart all networking agents.
whyWeak: It masks a path-specific failure, increases blast radius and supplies no causal proof.
